name: Gadolinium-iron-cobalt
equilibrium_context: Amorphous ferrimagnet, Gd and FeCo sublattices antiferromagnetically coupled, with magnetization and angular-momentum compensation points
summary: Special case: only the transient intermediate state qualifies for the registry, not the switching outcome.

driven_states.emergent_property: After a single femtosecond pulse the sublattices reverse on strongly different time scales; in the process a transient ferromagnet-like state arises for a few hundred femtoseconds, in which the Gd and Fe moments, antiparallel in equilibrium, stand parallel.
driven_states.source: Radu, Vahaplar, Stamm et al., Nature 472, 205 (2011), doi:10.1038/nature09901
driven_states.caveat: What qualifies for the registry here is exclusively the transient ferromagnet-like intermediate state, which is a genuine non-equilibrium state and appears nowhere in the phase diagram. The switching outcome itself is a symmetry-equivalent equilibrium state and is neither driven nor metastable - anyone listing it as a light-induced state would have to include every magnetization reversal by a field pulse. The intermediate state is measured element-resolved and reproduced; its microscopic description is not conclusively settled.

threshold.quantity: narrow fluence window: below it no switching, above it a multidomain state or damage

further_sources: Stanciu et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 99, 047601 (2007), doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.99.047601

gaps: The switched final state is deliberately NOT listed as a driven state.
